channel.description: The businesses hiding in plain sight.

item.title: Scholastic Book Fair: Who Really Makes the Money?
item.description: In its 2026 financial year, Scholastic's book fairs brought in $576.0 million, 36 cents of every dollar of revenue. A school chooses 25% in cash or 50% in Scholastic Dollars, and this is how the pop-up shop in the gym works.

item.title: How Do Gift Cards Make Money? Who Gets Paid
item.description: A supermarket sells gift cards for brands it does not own, and one middleman wires the whole rack. Here is how a $100 card splits, what happens to unused cards, and the company most shoppers have never heard of.

item.title: Who Owns the Pet Food Brands and Vet Clinics?
item.description: A candy company runs about 3,000 animal hospitals. A toothpaste company gets 23% of its sales from dog food. Why the brands in your kitchen are turning into pet companies.

item.title: How Hasbro Makes Money: Magic: The Gathering, Not Toys
item.description: Hasbro owns Monopoly, Transformers, Nerf and Play-Doh. But in 2025 about 88% of its profit came from one division: Wizards of the Coast, the home of Magic: The Gathering.

item.title: How Copart Makes Money From Wrecked Cars
item.description: What happens to a car after it is totaled? One company sells more than 4 million wrecks a year and keeps about 32 cents of every dollar as profit. The story of Copart.
